newsitem.title: USA: HMOs give little ground on Pacificare.
newsitem.headline: HMOs give little ground on Pacificare.

text.p: Stocks in major U.S. health maintenance organizations fell only slightly Friday, although shares in California HMO giant Pacificare Health Systems Inc plunged for the second time in five days.

By riding out Pacificare's problems with only minor damage, the sector reflects market confidence that Pacificare's problems are unique and largely related to its February acquisition of FHP International, analysts said.
At the same time, Pacificare's news that it will miss Wall Street earnings expectations by a wide margin may have fed some appetite for selling in the sector.
"People were looking for a reason for some profit-taking," said National Securities HMOs analyst Michael LeConey.

At midday, several major HMOs were off a bit, despite a broadly higher market: United HealthCare, off 1-1/4 at 52-7/8; Aetna Inc, off 2-9/16 at 104; WellPoint Health Networks Inc, off 1-7/8 at 46-1/8.
But none matched Pacificare's precipitous fall, off 8-3/16 at 60-7/8 at midday. On Tuesday, the broadly traded Pacificare Class B share closed at 66-3/4, down 18-3/4.

"From what Pacificare is saying, the indication is that the problems they're having are specific to Pacificare ... It's basically managing the FHP acquisition," said Josephthal Lyon & Ross HMOs analyst Mary O'Connell.
Pacificare completed a $2.2-billion acquisition of Santa Ana, Calif.-based FHP in February.
"The problems at FHP have proven to be more difficult than anybody anticipated," LeConey said.

Cypress, Calif.-based Pacificare announced Friday that it expects to report second-quarter net income of $0.30 to $0.45 per share, well shy of the $1.15 per share before pre-tax charges in the year-ago quarter.
Wall Street analysts had been expecting second-quarter 1997 earnings for Pacificare of about $1.16 per share.
